question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 1 & 16 \\ -1 & -2 & 10\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 1 & 16 \\ -1 & -2 & 10\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+1\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 1 & 16 \\ 0 & -1 & 26\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=-1\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 1 & 16 \\ 0 & 1 & -26\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y &=16 \\ y &=-26\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-26$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x+\left(-26\right)=16\,\Rightarrow\,x=16+26=42.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=42$ and $y=-26.$
